quests.hint: The numbered area at a train station where you wait to board.
quests.explanation: 'Platform number' is followed by a numeral, as in 'platform seven.' The word also means an online service in a tech context — 'a social media platform.'
quests.textToSpeak: The train to Edinburgh departs from ___ seven in approximately ten minutes.
quests.correctAnswer: The train to Edinburgh departs from platform seven in approximately ten minutes.

quests.hint: A printed or digital schedule showing when transport services run.
quests.explanation: 'Check the timetable' is the natural verb. The same word also describes a school's weekly class schedule.
quests.textToSpeak: She checked the bus ___ to find out when the last service of the day left.
quests.correctAnswer: She checked the bus timetable to find out when the last service of the day left.

quests.hint: A ticket that takes you there and brings you back again.
quests.explanation: 'A return ticket' goes both ways; 'a single' only goes one way. 'Day return' means the whole trip happens on the same day.
quests.textToSpeak: I need a ___ ticket to Oxford, please - I am coming back this evening.
quests.correctAnswer: I need a return ticket to Oxford, please - I am coming back this evening.

quests.hint: A step up to a better job or higher position at work.
quests.explanation: 'Get a promotion' or 'receive a promotion' both sound natural here. The verb form is 'promote' — 'she was promoted last year.'
quests.textToSpeak: After three years of hard work, she was delighted to receive the ___ she deserved.
quests.correctAnswer: After three years of hard work, she was delighted to receive the promotion she deserved.

quests.hint: Extra hours worked beyond your normal schedule.
quests.explanation: 'Work overtime' is the everyday way to say it. It's an uncountable noun, so we never say 'overtimes' or 'an overtime.'
quests.textToSpeak: He worked ___ every evening for a month to finish the project before the deadline.
quests.correctAnswer: He worked overtime every evening for a month to finish the project before the deadline.

quests.hint: The formal act of quitting a job.
quests.explanation: 'Hand in your resignation' or 'submit your resignation' are the everyday way to say it. The verb form is 'resign' — 'she resigned from her post.'
quests.textToSpeak: She handed in her ___ after receiving an exciting offer from a rival company.
quests.correctAnswer: She handed in her resignation after receiving an exciting offer from a rival company.

quests.hint: A live show put on for an audience, like music, dance, or theatre.
quests.explanation: 'Give a performance' or 'a live performance' are worth learning together. The verb form is 'perform.'
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ by the local orchestra last Saturday was absolutely breathtaking.
quests.correctAnswer: The performance by the local orchestra last Saturday was absolutely breathtaking.

quests.hint: A public display of art, photos, or objects for people to view.
quests.explanation: 'Hold an exhibition' or 'visit an exhibition' both work. Americans sometimes shorten it to 'exhibit.'
quests.textToSpeak: The photography ___ at the city gallery was open to the public for three weeks.
quests.correctAnswer: The photography exhibition at the city gallery was open to the public for three weeks.

quests.hint: The group of people watching or listening to a performance.
quests.explanation: The audience can take a singular or plural verb depending on context, much like 'family' or 'team.'
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ rose to their feet and gave the performers a wonderful standing ovation.
quests.correctAnswer: The audience rose to their feet and gave the performers a wonderful standing ovation.

quests.hint: Official belonging to a club, gym, or organisation, often paid for.
quests.explanation: 'Renew a membership' and 'gym membership' are the go-to phrases. 'Member' is the person; membership is the status itself.
quests.textToSpeak: She renewed her gym ___ for another year at the special discounted rate.
quests.correctAnswer: She renewed her gym membership for another year at the special discounted rate.

quests.hint: A regular, repeated payment for ongoing access to a service.
quests.explanation: 'A monthly subscription' and 'cancel a subscription' are the phrases you'll need most for streaming services, magazines, and apps.
quests.textToSpeak: His monthly ___ to the streaming service costs him twelve pounds each month.
quests.correctAnswer: His monthly subscription to the streaming service costs him twelve pounds each month.

quests.hint: Money knocked off the original price of something.
quests.explanation: 'A ten percent discount' or 'get a discount' are how most speakers actually say it. 'Discounted' is the adjective form — 'a discounted price.'
quests.textToSpeak: Students are entitled to a ten percent ___ on all full-price items in the store.
quests.correctAnswer: Students are entitled to a ten percent discount on all full-price items in the store.

quests.hint: Able to speak a language smoothly and confidently, without much hesitation.
quests.explanation: 'Become fluent in' a language is the key structure. 'Fluency' is the noun form of the same idea.
quests.textToSpeak: After two years living in Spain, she became completely ___ in Spanish.
quests.correctAnswer: After two years living in Spain, she became completely fluent in Spanish.

quests.hint: The particular way someone pronounces words, often revealing where they're from.
quests.explanation: 'Have an accent' is neutral — everyone has one! 'A strong accent' or 'a slight accent' describe how noticeable it is.
quests.textToSpeak: Her English was excellent, though she still had a noticeable French ___.
quests.correctAnswer: Her English was excellent, though she still had a noticeable French accent.

quests.hint: The full range of words a person knows and can use.
quests.explanation: 'Build your vocabulary' or 'a wide vocabulary' are the key expressions here. It's uncountable, so we never say 'a vocabulary' for one word.
quests.textToSpeak: Building a wide ___ is absolutely essential for becoming a confident speaker.
quests.correctAnswer: Building a wide vocabulary is absolutely essential for becoming a confident speaker.

quests.hint: A plan for how much money you can spend, and on what.
quests.explanation: 'On a tight budget' means spending carefully. As a verb, 'to budget' means planning your spending in advance.
quests.textToSpeak: They had to plan the holiday very carefully because their ___ was quite limited.
quests.correctAnswer: They had to plan the holiday very carefully because their budget was quite limited.

quests.hint: Having enough money to pay for something.
quests.explanation: 'Can't afford' is usually followed by a noun or 'to' plus a verb — 'can't afford the rent' or 'can't afford to travel.'
quests.textToSpeak: He could not ___ the rent in the city centre, so he moved further out.
quests.correctAnswer: He could not afford the rent in the city centre, so he moved further out.

quests.hint: Money set aside regularly instead of being spent.
quests.explanation: Savings is almost always plural. 'Savings account' is where this money is usually kept at a bank.
quests.textToSpeak: She put aside a small amount each month to gradually build up her ___.
quests.correctAnswer: She put aside a small amount each month to gradually build up her savings.

quests.hint: The particular taste that makes a food distinct.
quests.explanation: Flavour is spelled with a 'u' in British English ('flavor' in American English). 'Rich flavour' and 'strong flavour' both work equally well.
quests.textToSpeak: The soup had a wonderfully rich, smoky ___ from the roasted peppers.
quests.correctAnswer: The soup had a wonderfully rich, smoky flavour from the roasted peppers.

quests.hint: The amount of food served to one person.
quests.explanation: 'Portion size' is the phrase used to describe how much food you get. 'A generous portion' means more than expected.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ sizes at this restaurant are very generous - enough for two people.
quests.correctAnswer: The portion sizes at this restaurant are very generous - enough for two people.

quests.hint: One instalment of a TV series, part of a longer story.
quests.explanation: 'The final episode' or 'the next episode' are the pairings worth remembering. 'Binge-watch' means watching several episodes in a row.
quests.textToSpeak: The final ___ of the series left viewers with a completely unexpected ending.
quests.correctAnswer: The final episode of the series left viewers with a completely unexpected ending.

quests.hint: The secret combination of letters and numbers that protects your account.
quests.explanation: 'Create a password' or 'reset your password' are common tech phrases. 'A strong password' means one that's hard to guess.
quests.textToSpeak: You need to create a strong ___ that includes numbers and special characters.
quests.correctAnswer: You need to create a strong password that includes numbers and special characters.

quests.hint: Getting a file or app from the internet onto your own device.
quests.explanation: 'Download an app' is the opposite of 'upload,' which sends something from your device onto the internet.
quests.textToSpeak: You can ___ the app for free from the App Store or Google Play.
quests.correctAnswer: You can download the app for free from the App Store or Google Play.

quests.hint: Installing the latest version of an app or piece of software.
quests.explanation: 'Update your software' and 'a software update' are natural phrases, working as both verb and noun.
quests.textToSpeak: Make sure you ___ your software regularly to keep your device secure.
quests.correctAnswer: Make sure you update your software regularly to keep your device secure.

quests.hint: A formal statement expressing dissatisfaction about poor service or a problem.
quests.explanation: 'File a complaint' or 'make a complaint' both work. The verb form is 'complain' — 'she complained about the noise.'
quests.textToSpeak: She filed a formal ___ about the poor service she had received at the hotel.
quests.correctAnswer: She filed a formal complaint about the poor service she had received at the hotel.

quests.hint: A serious disagreement between two sides that can't easily agree.
quests.explanation: 'A legal dispute' and 'settle a dispute' are the more natural choice. As a verb, 'to dispute' means to formally disagree with a claim.
quests.textToSpeak: The two companies were involved in a lengthy legal ___ over intellectual property.
quests.correctAnswer: The two companies were involved in a lengthy legal dispute over intellectual property.

quests.hint: An agreement that finally ends a disagreement, often involving compensation.
quests.explanation: 'Reach a settlement' is the go-to phrase. The verb form is 'settle' — 'they settled out of court.'
quests.textToSpeak: After months of negotiation, they finally reached a fair ___ for all parties.
quests.correctAnswer: After months of negotiation, they finally reached a fair settlement for all parties.

quests.hint: A short, personal story told to entertain or make a point.
quests.explanation: 'Share an anecdote' or 'tell an anecdote' are what you'll hear in everyday speech. It's usually true and personal, unlike a fictional 'tale.'
quests.textToSpeak: She shared a funny ___ about getting completely lost on her first day in the city.
quests.correctAnswer: She shared a funny anecdote about getting completely lost on her first day in the city.

quests.hint: The quality of being funny, or the ability to find things funny.
quests.explanation: Humour is spelled with a 'u' in British English ('humor' in American English). 'Sense of humour' is the phrase you'll hear constantly.
quests.textToSpeak: His wonderful sense of ___ made him very popular and easy to get along with.
quests.correctAnswer: His wonderful sense of humour made him very popular and easy to get along with.

quests.hint: The skill of telling stories in a way that captures people's attention.
quests.explanation: 'A gift for storytelling' is a lovely way to praise someone's skill. The word combines 'story' and 'telling' into one compound noun.
quests.textToSpeak: She has a remarkable gift for ___ that keeps audiences completely engaged.
quests.correctAnswer: She has a remarkable gift for storytelling that keeps audiences completely engaged.
